name: Tolvaptan
lead: Tolvaptan is a selective vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist that causes aquaresis, the excretion of free water without major loss of electrolytes. It is used to treat clinically significant hyponatremia (brand Samsca) and to slow kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (brand Jynarque). [1][2]

It is listed on the wiki under depuffing because of its water-excreting effect. No published study has tested tolvaptan for facial puffiness or appearance, and no community discussion was available to document.

The Jynarque label carries a boxed warning for serious and potentially fatal liver injury, with acute liver failure requiring transplantation reported, and requires monthly liver-test monitoring early in treatment. [2]

paras: Hyponatremia: tolvaptan is approved for clinically significant euvolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia, including cases from heart failure, cirrhosis and SIADH, and Grokipedia states treatment is started in hospital and limited in duration because of liver risk. [1] ADPKD: the Jynarque label indicates it to slow kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing disease. [2]

Tolvaptan binds the V2 receptor with an affinity the label puts at 1.8 times that of native vasopressin and 29 times its affinity for the V1a receptor. Blocking vasopressin lowers adenylate cyclase activity and cAMP in the kidney's collecting duct, reducing water reabsorption. [2] Reviews of the vaptan class describe such non-peptide vasopressin antagonists. [3]

The label's boxed warning concerns serious liver injury. It also warns of hypernatremia, dehydration and hypovolemia, and of interactions with CYP3A inhibitors. [2] Embryo-fetal studies in animals showed no developmental toxicity at maternally non-toxic doses, and human data are insufficient. [2]
No studies found on tolvaptan for facial puffiness or cosmetic depuffing. Published trials cover hyponatremia, heart failure and polycystic kidney disease.

Two multicenter placebo-controlled trials (SALT) tested tolvaptan in euvolemic or hypervolemic hyponatremia with 448 patients. [4] The EVEREST trials examined it in patients hospitalised for worsening heart failure. [5][6] The TEMPO 3:4 trial randomised 1,445 adults with ADPKD for three years, and a later NEJM study examined later-stage disease. [7][8]

timeline.event: Double-blind trial of V2 blockade with tolvaptan in chronic heart failure published. [9]
EVEREST outcome and clinical status trials published. [5][6]
US approval of Samsca, according to Grokipedia. [1]

card.summary: A prescription vasopressin blocker that makes the body excrete free water; it is approved for hyponatremia and kidney disease, with a boxed liver-injury warning and no appearance data.
card.note: Boxed warning for serious liver injury; requires monitoring.

quick.overview:
Tolvaptan is a prescription drug that blocks vasopressin's action in the kidney so more free water leaves in urine. It is approved for low blood sodium and for slowing polycystic kidney disease.

It appears under depuffing because of this water-excreting effect, but nobody has studied it for facial puffiness.
quick.mechanism: It antagonizes the V2 vasopressin receptor in the collecting duct, reducing cAMP and water reabsorption, an effect called aquaresis.
quick.risks: The Jynarque label has a boxed warning for serious, potentially fatal liver injury and warns of dehydration and abnormally high sodium. It interacts with CYP3A inhibitors and is prescription-only.
